Remember that you told me that one night you double folded the bedding and finding it soft, Rasulullaah ﷺ slept through the night and woke up only with Bilaal's Adhaan. He then said to you, 'O Hafsah! What have you done? You had double folded the bedding last night, causing sleep to carry me through to the morning. What need have I for this world? Why do you preoccupy me with soft beds?' O Hafsah! Don't you know that all Rasulullaah ﷺ's earlier and later error had been forgiven? Yet he went hungry in the evenings, spent his sleeping hours in Sajdah and remained in Ruku, Sajdah, weeping and humbling himself before Allaah throughout the hours of the day and night. This he did until the day Allaah took him into the fold of His mercy and pleasure. Umar shall never eat good foods, and shall never wear fine clothing because he has a perfect example in his two companions (Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)). He shall also never eat two meals at the same time except for having salt and olive oil together. He shall eat meat only once a month just so that his month passes like the masses."
The two ladies then left and informed the Sahabah (RA) about what had transpired. Hadhrat Umar (RA) remained like this until he eventually left to meet Allaah.[^1]

Hadhrat Ikrama bin Khaalid narrates that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA), Hadhrat Ibn Mutee (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once addressed Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "If you eat good food, it would give you more strength to establish the truth." Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "I know well that each of you wish me well, but I have left my two companions Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) on a certain route and if I leave that route, I shall not be able to meet them at the destination."[^2]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah bin Sahl bin Hunayf (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah bin Sahl bin Hunayf (RA) says that for a long period of time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) took nothing from the Baytul Maal. He eventually reached a stage where he started suffering poverty (because involvement in public matters gave him no time to engage in trade). He then sent for some of the Sahabah (RA) to consult with them. He addressed them saying, "My task has preoccupied me (from earning), so what (allowance) do you see appropriate for me?" Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) replied, "(So much) That you are able to eat and feed others as well." Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl (RA) echoed the opinion. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked Hadhrat Ali (RA), "What have you to say about it?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "(So much that is sufficient for your) Morning and evening meals." Hadhrat Umar (RA) abided by this opinion.[^3]
